question.text: While making an application to SEBI for a No Objection Certificate (NOC) for FPI surrender, the DDP must confirm that:

answer.text: The FPI has published a notice in two national newspapers
The FPI has informed all its investors about the surrender
The FPI has obtained consent from all stock exchanges where it traded
The FPI accounts have nil balance, are blocked for further transactions, and there are no pending dues/fees towards SEBI

explanation.text: The Logic: For an FPI surrender NOC, the DDP must confirm three items per the workbook: (i) the FPI accounts have nil balance and are blocked for further transactions, and the CP code is blocked; (ii) there are no dues or fees pending towards SEBI; and (iii) there are no actions or proceedings pending against the FPI. Following NOC, the FPI account is closed and the CP code is deactivated. The Trap: A newspaper notice is not a surrender NOC requirement under the FPI framework. Investor intimation and exchange consent are also not part of the three NOC checks. Note: The three NOC checks together form a closure-readiness test - account-level (nil balance/blocked), financial (no SEBI dues), and legal (no pending proceedings).
